result.summary: Subclasses Python's `http.client.HTTPConnection` in the functional test framework to apply `set_ephemeral_port_range()` on newly created client sockets before connecting. Replaces direct `http.client.HTTPConnection` instantiations in the RPC auth proxy and several functional tests with this wrapper to avoid ephemeral port overlap on BSD systems.
result.problem: On FreeBSD and OpenBSD, the default ephemeral port ranges overlap with the functional test suite's reserved port range. Because Python's standard `http.client` manages its own socket creation internally, it bypasses the test framework's `set_ephemeral_port_range()` socket option, allowing outgoing HTTP/RPC connections directed to closed ports to select identical local ports and connect to themselves.
evidence: Author encountered this while stress-testing FreeBSD CI in #36147: "the wrong-RPC-port startup check failed with BadStatusLine: POST / HTTP/1.1 because the client read back its own request."
result.changed_since_previous: None; the previous entry was generated without a diff patch.
result.card: Subclasses Python's HTTPConnection in the functional test framework to configure ephemeral port ranges before establishing connections. On FreeBSD and OpenBSD, default ephemeral port ranges overlap with test ports, causing http.client sockets to occasionally assign identical source and destination ports and connect to themselves when targeting closed ports. The author encountered this while stress-testing native FreeBSD CI in #36147, where a wrong-RPC-port startup check failed with BadStatusLine after reading its own request. This change stabilizes functional test runs on BSD platforms and unblocks native FreeBSD CI in #36147.

risk.why: Touches only functional test framework networking wrappers; a regression would cause test suite connection failures.
